title: Capacity runbook: per-commitment-window slicing (Q1-Q2 2027)
body:
Sheet: Per-Contract Capacity Slicing Runbook

Overview:
This runbook captures per-contract dedicated GPU reservations across regions for the Q1->Q2 2027 commitment window. Intended as a working planning artifact (not final billing ledger). Focus: minimize customer-facing disruption during phasing, ensure regional headroom and clear fallback policy.

Legend for columns: ContractID | Customer | Committed_GPUs | GPU_Type | Primary_Region | Secondary_Region | Allocation_Window | Baseline_Tokens_s | Peak_Tokens_s | Utilization_Target_pct | Current_Alloc_pct | Suggested_Phaseing (months:Jan-Feb-Mar-Apr-May-Jun) | Notes / Risks

Rows:
RC-1007 | AtlasML | 48 | H100-80GB | us-west1 | europe-west1 | 2027-01-01->2027-06-30 | 12500 | 42000 | 65 | 100 | 30/30/40/0/0/0 | initial committed pool; customer expects burstable Q1; SLA hard cap 48 but allow overcommit buffer 10% across region
RC-1012 | NeoCommerce | 12 | A100-40GB | europe-west1 | europe-north1 | 2027-02-01->2027-04-30 | 3200 | 9600 | 70 | 100 | 50/50/0/0/0/0 | planned canary rollout in Feb; prefer strict regional residency (no fallback outside EU)
RC-1029 | FinSight | 96 | H100-80GB | us-east4 | us-central1 | 2027-01-15->2027-06-30 | 28000 | 98000 | 80 | 80 | 20/30/30/20/0/0 | high utilization customer; recommend reserved standby capacity for transactional spikes; negotiate soft cap agreement
RC-1034 | EduPrompt | 6 | L4 | asia-southeast1 | us-west1 | 2027-03-01->2027-05-31 | 600 | 2400 | 50 | 100 | 0/25/25/25/25/0 | APAC latency-sensitive; allow short burst to us-west1 if APAC saturated (audit + data path review)
RC-1041 | HealthSync | 24 | A100-80GB | europe-west1 | us-east4 | 2027-01-01->2027-03-31 | 4800 | 14400 | 60 | 100 | 40/30/30/0/0/0 | requires SOC2+ audit path; any cross-region fallback requires ticket and encryption proof

Phasing rules summary:
- Phase percentages map to fraction of committed GPUs physically pinned to region/month. Remaining capacity is available for pooled cross-contract overcommit buffer.
- Soft cap: up to 10% overcommit of physical GPUs is allowed for short bursts if customers have not exceeded utilization target and if SLOs of others can be honored.
- Hard cap: absolute committed GPUs per contract must never drop below 90% of contractual SLA for >6 hours without CS escalation.

Regional headroom table:
Region | Total_Physical_GPUs | Reserved_for_Dedicated | Pooled_Headroom | Expected_util_peak_week | Notes
us-west1 | 256 | 132 | 24 | Mon-Fri 18:00-22:00 PST | primary for west coast customers; watch ML benchmarks after H100 kernel update on 2027-02-10
europe-west1 | 208 | 96 | 16 | Weekdays 09:00-17:00 CET | EU residency constraints for some contracts
us-east4 | 192 | 88 | 8 | Mon-Fri 12:00-18:00 ET | planned cluster expansion in May 2027 (+48 GPUs)
asia-southeast1 | 80 | 18 | 6 | Weekends 00:00-04:00 SGT | limited capacity - use as secondary fallback only

Fallback & hot-swap matrix:
Trigger | Action | Time budget | Escalation
Capacity spike > planned peak | borrow pooled_headroom in same region; if insufficient, trigger cross-region fallback to secondary_region | target < 5 minutes to shift traffic via routing | on-call infra -> lead-tech -> customer CS notified within 30 mins
Node failure (rack-level) | shift affected shards to other racks in same AZ; if AZ impacted >10% capacity, redistribute affected contracts across other regions with sticky routing | target < 30 minutes | SRE oncall + infra manager
Overcommit exhaustion | throttle best-effort customers defined in soft-cap list; start percentage=20% reduction | immediate | Product ops + CS coordinate

Action items (owner -> due):
- Validate per-contract GPU affinity tags in provisioning pipeline (Ravi Kapur -> 2027-01-20)
- Add enforcement for hard cap alarms at 90% contract breach (Lina Gomez -> 2027-01-18)
- Run synthetic burst test across us-west1 cluster w/ H100 kernel v2 (Marcus Chen -> 2027-02-05)
- Confirm EU-only fallback legal review for NeoCommerce (CS lead Aisha Patel -> 2027-01-25)

Decision log (working):
- 2026-12-08: agreed to use 10% pooled overcommit buffer for Q1 to accommodate onboarding churn (decision by infra leads)
- 2026-12-20: designated us-west1 as primary for AtlasML due to token distribution analysis

Open questions:
- Should pooled_headroom be rebalanced monthly vs fixed for full commitment window? (ops cost vs flexibility)
- For customers requiring strict regional residency, can we offer paid standby nodes in a separate availability domain?

Notes to reviewers: this is a working planning sheet intended for infra + solutions + CS to align on physical pinning and escalation SLAs. Update suggested phased allocations after the Jan synthetic test and before Feb 1st customer cutovers.
